newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Asian Metals - S.Korean demand cooled by Jinro woes.
newsitem.headline: Asian Metals - S.Korean demand cooled by Jinro woes.

text.p: The financial troubles of South Korea's 19th largest conglomerate Jinro Group have cast a shadow over activity in the domestic metal industry, already battered by the collapse of two steel makers and labour unrest, traders in Seoul said.
"Jinro's financial trouble has dampened market sentiment, together with the collapse of Hanbo Steel and Sammi Steel," a trader with Ssangyong Corp said.
Metal traders were cautious of further developments about the Jinro Group, especially about Jinro Industries Co Ltd, an affiliate of the Jinro Group and an electric cable manufacturer.
Jinro Industries has produced 33,000 tonnes of electric cable a year.
"There has been no change in the company up to now although our group is in financial trouble," a senior official of Jinro Industries said.
The Jinro official said it was scheduled to start producing 30,000 tonnes of South Copper Wire Rod (SCR) a year from April. "The SCR production will soon start," he said.
Meanwhile, South Korea's Office of Supply (OSROK) invited tenders to buy 1,550 tonnes of high grade aluminium ingot by 2:00 p.m. (0500 GMT) on Friday.
"It is a good indication of lagging local aluminium demand as the (tender) amount is far less than before although the market is in tight supply," another trader with Ssangyong Corp said.
The amount offered by suppliers has fallen by more than 50 percent, reflecting current physical tightness in the Far Eastern aluminium market, the second Ssangyong trader said.
A Japanese trader based in Tokyo said recent physical tightness in the regional aluminium market was well reflected by recent strong Japanese aluminium import premiums for nearby shipment.
"At the moment, the alumnium import premium is hovering at about $90 a tonne for the second quarter shipment due to tight supply situation," the Japanese trader said.
Import premiums for the third quarter shipment were expected to fall $7 to $10 a tonne from the second quarter, the Japanese trader said.
Aluminium import premiums for spot delivery were seen flat at a range of $85-$90 a tonne CIF Pusan over LME's cash prices, traders said.
Domestic aluminium prices were flat at 1.52 million won a tonne over the past week and copper prices were unchanged at 2.345 million won a tonne.
Domestic zinc prices were unchanged at 1.230 million won a tonne over the past week, while lead prices fell to 690,000 won a tonne from 744,000 won a week ago.
Traders said the import premium for Chinese special high grade zinc for nearby shipment had fallen to $30 to $35 a tonne due to recent gains on the LME, compared to $35 to $40 a tonne a week earlier.
